title: Proactive Eval Executor for Tenant-Prioritized Pin Upgrades
creator: Marco Li
description:
Goal: Build an automated evaluation executor that triggers lightweight, tenant-prioritized quality checks whenever a model version is pinned or upgraded in either the public catalog or a customer-locked configuration. This will reduce silent regressions slipping into production and surface degradations before a rollout reaches significant traffic.

Background: We already run heavier post-promotion evals in several projects, but customers and catalog owners need a fast, cost-aware preflight / post-pin probe that is: tenant-aware (higher-usage tenants get earlier or stricter checks), budget-sensible (uses a configurable cost budget per tenant / catalog change), and integrated with rollout automation (can gate canaries or flag for manual review).

Scope & non-goals:
 - In-scope: automated trigger, sampling policy, lightweight probe definitions (smoke + fidelity delta), tenant prioritization rules, gating signals for Console/Deploy workflows, alerting hooks, basic dashboarding.
 - Out-of-scope: full synthetic fleet (this will reuse existing probe runner infra), long-running large-sample A/B experiments, or automated rollback enforcement (we will surface signals and optionally mark a release as blocked; rollback still manual for MVP).

Key behaviors and rules:
 1) Trigger points: catalog model version push, catalog model pin, customer tenant pin/upgrade.
 2) Tenant prioritization: tenants with "high" usage or SLA flag are scheduled first and receive a larger sample budget. Low-usage tenants get a tiny smoke sample. Priority tiers come from the tenant metadata store.
 3) Sampling & cost guard: each trigger carries a default cost budget (tokens + compute time). The eval executor enforces sampling caps and backpressure if budget exceeded. Admins can override per-tenant budgets.
 4) Probe types: lightweight smoke (sanity/latency), fidelity delta (selected T0 prompts from representative prompt bank), and safety quick checks (token-level heuristics). Only run higher-fidelity checks for high-priority tenants or when deltas exceed thresholds.
 5) Signal scoring: produce a composite score (delta_fidelity, latency_pct_change, safety_alert_count). Provide a pass/warn/fail outcome and a delta report.
 6) Integration: results push to Console -> Rollout page, emit webhook to tenant integrations, and create an internal alert (Slack/Pager duty routing) for fail/warn on high-priority tenants.

Implementation approach (MVP):
 - Phase 1 (MVP): lightweight executor service that listens to pin events, loads tenant priority & budget, schedules probe runner with constrained sample sets, computes delta metrics, emits a standardized result envelope. No auto-rollback.
 - Phase 2: add staged escalation (broader sample if initial warn), automated gating hooks for canary promotion pipelines, and cost analytics.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
 - % of tenant pin events that run an automated eval within 10 minutes: target 90%
 - % of detected regressions that are triaged before reaching 1% production traffic: target 75%
 - Average token cost per triggered eval (clustered by priority): remain under configured budget for 95% of runs

Open questions & trade-offs:
 - How large should the default sample bank be for multi-lingual models? (estimate: 50–200 prompts depending on model size)
 - When to escalate from smoke to deeper checks? We propose threshold-based escalation on relative latency or top-k answer divergence.
 - Should we allow customers to opt out of automatic pin-triggered evals? (propose opt-out flag but warn about risk)

Next steps / action items:
 - PM to align with Eng on event contract for pin events and required tenant metadata (owner: Marco, due: 2026-03-05).
 - Eng to prototype executor that can schedule a 20-prompt smoke run under budget (owner: Priya Raman, due: 2026-03-20).
 - Design to mock Console UI for results and gating controls (owner: Lena Ortiz, due: 2026-03-18).

Notes: We should avoid duplicating heavy eval workloads already scheduled by the catalog pipeline; this executor must be cheap and fast by design. We will iterate on signal thresholds after 1 month of live runs.
